# APPROVED-SET GRANDFATHER MANIFEST (frozen 2026-08-11, Codex High round 14)
#
# The approved-set binding rule used to be scoped by a filename timestamp
# cutoff. The stamp in a migration's filename is chosen by whoever writes the
# file, so a brand-new migration named with an older stamp landed on the
# "history" side of the cutoff and was never checked at all -- the guard was
# switched off by the very input it was guarding.
#
# This manifest replaces that cutoff. It lists, by content hash, every
# migration that existed at the moment the rule landed. A migration is treated
# as history ONLY if its basename appears here AND its bytes still hash to the
# recorded value. Everything else -- every newly added file, whatever it is
# named, and every edit to a file listed here -- is in force.
#
# It is FROZEN. Do not append a new migration to it: adding a row here exempts
# that migration from the rule and is a deliberate, reviewed act. Regenerating
# it wholesale would silently re-exempt whatever had drifted since.
#
# Hashes are sha256 over the file with carriage returns removed, so a CRLF
# checkout on Windows and an LF checkout on Linux agree.
#
# Format: <sha256>  <basename>

#
# The row below is history that has not reached main yet. It is already applied
# to the live database but still sits on an open branch, so it was not in the
# working tree when this manifest was frozen. It rewrites commission rows
# without an approved-set binding: once it merges it would be a "new" file, go
# in force, and red-build main for everyone. The write it performs has already
# happened in production and the file must not be edited (a migration that has
# been applied is immutable), so an exemption is the only honest option.
#
# The exemption is pinned to the exact bytes on that branch. If the file is
# amended before it merges the hash stops matching and the rule goes back in
# force, which is the correct outcome -- an amended migration is a new one.
